findings.title: Renaming a settings-owned MCP server drops supported non-editor fields
findings.trigger: A supported hand-edited settings-owned server has connectTimeoutMs, connectRetries or inlineImages, and the user changes only its name to an unused valid name in the full editor.
findings.expected: Transfer existing supported, unedited options to the renamed configuration.
findings.actual: The new map key receives only editor-authored fields and the old key is deleted, so supported extra options disappear. Same-name saves retain them through recursive merge.
findings.cause: A partial edit patch is reused as the complete replacement record when changing the enclosing server key.
counterevidence: The editor field whitelist is intentional; the defect is incomplete record transfer across rename.
Same-name deepMerge preserves unedited fields and is outside this failure condition.
Plugin override locks server identity and is excluded.
Supported manual settings entry is documented in schema-export, with real schema/DTO consumers; arbitrary unknown fields are not assumed supported.
findings.validation: Static ordinary supported config producer, full edit/name/save and merge paths, plus independent counterevidence; zero function/helper/language fixture/test/form/config/MCP/process/network execution. No runtime connection or image result claimed.
findings.remediation: Transfer existing supported non-editor configuration when renaming, then apply the editable-field patch; keep tombstone and origin contracts and avoid persisting UI metadata.
findings.classificationNote: Completes the explicitly unclassified rename-extra-fields boundary from Round38. One P3 static issue; distinct from MCP-R38-01 args serialization, no duplicate item or absolute-first claim.
